findings: An infiltrative pancreatic cancer measuring 55 mm is observed in the body of the pancreas. Serosal invasion and retropancreatic tissue invasion are noted. There is contact of more than 180° with the splenic artery, suggesting invasion. The tumor is in contact with the aorta, with an indistinct boundary, indicating invasion. No other local invasion factors are identified. No lymph node metastases are present. Two hypodense masses are observed in the right lobe of the liver, raising suspicion of liver metastases.

responses.content:
Task 1: Diagnose the local invasion factors of pancreatic cancer.

CH0 (no invasion of the common hepatic artery)
DU0 (no invasion of the duodenum)
S1 (serosal invasion)
RP1 (retropancreatic tissue invasion)
PV0 (no invasion of the portal vein)
A1 (invasion of the splenic artery)
PL0 (no invasion of the pancreatic duct)
OO1 (invasion of the aorta)

Task 2: Determine the classification for local invasion (T classification) of pancreatic cancer.

Based on the size of the tumor (55 mm) and the presence of serosal invasion, retropancreatic tissue invasion, invasion of the splenic artery, and invasion of the aorta, the T classification is T4.

Task 3: Determine the N classification of pancreatic cancer.

Regional lymph nodes for pancreatic cancer in the body of the pancreas are:
- Station 12 (left gastric artery)
- Station 13 (common hepatic artery)
- Station 14 (proper hepatic artery)
- Station 15 (gastroduodenal artery)
- Station 16 (common bile duct)
- Station 17 (cystic duct)
- Station 18 (hilar lymph nodes)
- Station 19 (pericholedochal lymph nodes)
- Station 20 (peripancreatic lymph nodes)

No metastatic lymph nodes are present in the regional stations. Therefore, the N classification is N0.

Task 4: Determine the M classification of pancreatic cancer.

Distant metastases are present in the liver, so the M classification is M1.

Task 5: Determine the resectability classification of pancreatic cancer.

The presence of distant metastases (M1) qualifies as non-resectable. Therefore, the resectability classification is Unresectable (UR).

Task 6: Determine the overall stage according to the JPS staging system.

Based on the T classification (T4), N classification (N0), and M classification (M1), the overall stage is Stage IV.
